claims.text: Near-equiatomic HEAs can form single-phase FCC or BCC solid solutions stabilized by high configurational entropy.
DSC can measure heat capacity through the approach to melting.
DSC can identify melting-transition temperatures in compositionally complex alloys.
DSC directly provides the latent heat and hence fusion enthalpy.
Fusion entropy can be obtained by integrating heat-capacity data.
High-temperature dilatometry can quantify the volume change at melting in HEAs.
Heating at approximately 5–10 K/min approaches near-equilibrium melting conditions.
An inert atmosphere and homogenized single-phase samples minimize oxidation and secondary-phase precipitation during measurement.
Configurational entropy contributes substantially to the entropy and Gibbs free energy of multicomponent alloys.
Atomic-scale heterogeneities inherent to HEAs influence their melting behavior.
Entropy gained through multicomponent mixing can lower the liquid Gibbs free energy and depress melting temperature.
CALPHAD can evaluate phase stability by balancing enthalpic and entropic contributions to Gibbs free energy.
DSC and dilatometry datasets can be used together to refine an HEA-specific CALPHAD model for fusion properties.
The updated CALPHAD framework can determine selected liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the HEA family.
The integrated approach will predict HEA melting temperatures within approximately ±10 K.
The integrated approach will determine fusion enthalpy and entropy within approximately ±5–10% of independent measurements.
The integrated approach will reliably capture the volume change at melting.
Isolated DSC and static computational models typically have larger deviations and lower throughput because configurational mixing effects are underrepresented.
The method is less reliable for systems with non-equilibrium behavior, kinetic limitations, secondary-phase precipitation, or strong short-range ordering.
Preliminary evidence supports the stated ±10 K and ±5–10% error margins.

contradictions.description: The intervention says the DSC and dilatometry datasets are fed into and used to refine the CALPHAD model, whereas the validation design describes the CALPHAD predictions as independent of the measurements. Without a held-out calibration/validation split, these statements are methodologically inconsistent.
